newsitem.title: UK: Monthly Review - HK is ceded; left wins in France.
newsitem.headline: Monthly Review - HK is ceded; left wins in France.

text.p: Britain ceded Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30 amid pledges from Beijing's communist leaders to respect the special status of the economic powerhouse and worries from pro-democracy groups that their freedom might be curtailed.
In France, Socialist Lionel Jospin became prime minister after a general election and reshaped expectations for the run-up to the introduction of a European single currency.
Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot, responsible for more than a million deaths in Cambodia during his 1975-79 Maoist reign of terror, was finally captured by a breakaway faction of his own group.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
Jun 1 - The combined left, spearheaded by Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, clinch victory in the French general election after the second round of voting.
Jun 2 - Nigerian gunboats bombard Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, as fighting rages between Nigerian troops intervening to reverse a military coup and soldiers and rebel allies.
Jun 2 - Romania and Ukraine put decades of mistrust behind them by signing a long-delayed border treaty.
Jun 2 - Timothy McVeigh is found guilty on all counts in the bombing of a federal building in Oklahoma City in 1995 that killed 168 people. On June 13 he is sentenced to death.
Jun 3 - Israel's opposition Labour party elects former army chief Ehud Barak as its new leader.
Jun 4 - An Indian judge drops charges against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a forgery trial.
Jun 4 - Tens of thousands of Hong Kong people flock to a local park to honour the victims of Beijing's bloody 1989 crackdown in Tiananmen Square.
Jun 4 - The U.N. Security Council votes unanimously to approve a six-month renewal of its "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq.
Jun 4 - Richard Holbrooke, credited with bringing Bosnia's warring parties together to sign the Dayton agreement, is appointed special U.S. emissary for Cyprus.
Jun 5 - Confessed CIA double-agent Harold Nicholson is sentenced to 23 years and seven months in prison for spying for Russia.
Jun 5 - Fighting breaks out in Congo's capital Brazzaville after troops surround the home of former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.
Jun 6 - Close allies of President Liamine Zeroual sweep to victory in Algeria's new parliament.
Jun 6 - Caoimhghin O Caolain wins a seat in Ireland's election becoming the first member of Sinn Fein, political wing of the IRA guerrilla group, to enter Ireland's parliament.
Jun 7 - Burundi's ousted civilian president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya leaves the U.S. embassy in the capital Bujumbura after almost a year.
Jun 7 - Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia recapture the strategic town of Jabal os-Siraj north of Kabul.

Jun 9 - France's new government disconcerts Germany and other EU allies by saying it needs time to consider a pact on budget deficits which has already been agreed and is intended to be a cornerstone of a future EU single currency.
Jun 9 - France sends 800 extra troops to Brazzaville and evacuates hundreds of French citizens.
Jun 10 - Pope John Paul II leaves Poland after an 11-day pilgrimage to his homeland.
Jun 11 - A government commission approves a move to allow Vittorio Emanuele, the son of Italy's last king, to return home from a 50-year exile from January 1, 1998.
Jun 12 - The United States informs NATO it wants to invite only Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to join the alliance in a first wave of eastward expansion.
Jun 12 - President Mary Robinson of Ireland is named to the top U.N. human rights post by Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Jun 13 - Reports emerge that ailing Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot has killed his defence chief Son Sen and 11 members of his family, and fled his northern stronghold. On June 16 most of his remaining fighters are reported to have deserted him and he is said to be heading for the Thai border.
Jun 15 - Israel's High Court rejects a petition demanding that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu be indicted for fraud.
Jun 15 - In Colombia, leftist rebels end Latin America's longest-running hostage crisis when they release 70 soldiers and marines they took prisoner last August and January.
Jun 15 - Franjo Tudjman is re-elected Croatian president.

Jun 16 - EU leaders meeting in Amsterdam approve a controversial budget pact intended to guarantee the stability of the future single currency and a resolution on boosting employment and growth. They finally agree revisions to the Maastricht union treaty in the early hours of June 18.
Jun 17 - South African white supremacist Eugene Terre Blanche is sentenced to six years in jail for trying to murder one black man and assaulting another.
Jun 17 - Johnny Paul Koroma, the leader of Sierra Leone's military coup, is sworn in as head of state.
Jun 17 - Warring parties in Congo agree a three-day truce and the demilitarisation of Brazzaville airport. On June 20 they extend it for a further week.
Jun 18 - Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigns under pressure from the secularist army.
Jun 18 - Robert Kennedy's assassin, Sirhan Sirhan, is denied parole for the 10th time.
Jun 18 - U.S. indicts Saudi dissident Hani al-Sayegh on conspiracy and murder charges.
Jun 19 - The prime ministers of India and Pakistan speak for the first time on the "hotline" set up to dispel mistrust between the two states.
Jun 19 - Two activists are found guilty of libelling hamburger giant McDonald's at the end of the longest trial in English legal history
Jun 19 - William Hague becomes the youngest leader of Britain's Conservative Party in nearly 200 years.
Jun 20 - Felipe Gonzalez announces he will not seek re-election as secretary general of the Spanish Socialist party. The party chooses veteran Joaquin Almunia for the job on June 22.
Jun 20 - Forty people are wounded in the fiercest day in a week of clashes between Palestinians and Israel soldiers in Hebron, taking the total for seven days of violence to over 120.
Jun 20 - Kocheril Raman Narayanan wins the support of the three main parties in India, appearing to ensure he will win the July 14 presidential election.

Jun 20 - About 200 people stage a rare protest in Beijing against housing policies. It is the first known protest since the 1989 pro-democracy protest on Tiananmen Square which ended in a massacre of demonstrators.
Jun 20 - Ahead of the summit in the United States of the Group of Seven major industrial powers and Russia, Moscow pledges to stop targeting Japan with its nuclear missiles.

Jun 20 - The U.S. tobacco industry agrees with state authorities to pay $368.5 billion in damages and submit to tougher regulation in order to avert a wave of lawsuits over the health effects of smoking.
Jun 20 - President Boris Yeltsin announces that Russia has been admitted to the Paris Club of creditor nations.
Jun 21 - The Cambodian government confirms that Pol Pot has been captured by former comrades who have turned against him.
Jun 22 - Under U.S. pressure, the Group of Seven summit ends with a compromise on global warming that disappoints European leaders.
Jun 24 - Turkey's two rival conservative leaders fail to agree on forging a secularist alliance under the leadership of prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz.
Jun 24 - The House of Representatives votes by a large majority to support President Clinton's decision to renew China's Most Favoured Nation trade status for another year.
Jun 25 - Swiss banks agree to have Holocaust-era claims resolved by an independent panel and not by the banks themselves.
Jun 25 - British Prime Minister Tony Blair unveils far-reaching proposals for rival Northern Irish guerrillas to disarm concurrently with talks on a political settlement.
Jun 25 - Russia's Mir space station collides with a cargo craft during a manual docking exercise.
Jun 25 - President Clinton says he has approved strong new clean air standards to reduce pollution and protect public health.
Jun 26 - Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern is elected Prime Minister of a minority Irish government.
Jun 27 - Sierra Leone's neighbours opt for dialogue and economic sanctions to force its military rulers to reinstate ousted civilian President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

Jun 27 - French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn says Paris will not cut its budget deficit to 3.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product this year, shifting the goalposts for entry to European monetary union.
Jun 27 - Danish High Court rejects a suit by a group of Danes who say the country's European Union membership is unconstitutional.
Jun 27 - Tajikistan's President Imomali Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri sign an historic peace accord to end four years of civil war.
Jun 27 - Ninety-five countries agree at a conference in Brussels to sign up to a ban on landmines.
Jun 27 - Three people are killed and seven injured when an explosion rips through a train travelling from Moscow to St Petersburg.
Jun 28 - The week-long United Nations Earth Summit ends early with its chairman delivering the verdict: "Our words have not been matched by deeds."
Jun 28 - A four-day truce comes into force in the Central African Republic capital Bangui after a week of bloody clashes between African peacekeepers and disaffected soldiers.
Jun 29 - Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa says his administration will hold elections next May.
Jun 30 - President Sali Berisha concedes his Democratic Party have lost a general election in Albania.
Jun 30 - Britain's Prince Charles hands Hong Kong back to China at the stroke of midnight, closing another chapter of Britain's once mighty empire.

Notable deaths in June included: Helen Jacobs, U.S. tennis player (2nd); Li Shuxian, widow of the last Chinese Emperor Pu Yi (10); Son Sen, Khmer Rouge defence chief (10); Vittorio Mussolini, son of the Italian dictator (12); Edmond Leburton, former Belgian prime minister (15); John Akii-Bua, Uganda's only Olympic gold medallist (20); Fidel Velazquez, Mexican union leader (21); Betty Shabazz, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X (23); Jacques Cousteau, French marine explorer (25).
